decision: Migrations applied by psql (--single-transaction, ON_ERROR_STOP) instead of psycopg

decision: The statement is named by its line number (where it ends), not quoted

decision: auth.uid/role/jwt read only request.jwt.claims; T-02's legacy request.jwt.claim.sub fallback dropped

decision: auth.users is a subset of Supabase's columns, with defaults for aud, role and metadata

decision: No USAGE grant on extensions and no PostgREST db-extra-search-path; USAGE on auth kept
why: Policies and defaults store resolved objects, so mutants showed no difference; auth USAGE is needed for a direct auth.uid() call (T-02's test)

decision: auth.users is seeded because tables reference it, not listed explicitly
why: An unreferenced auth.users has no effect on an anon attack

decision: Tables in other schemas that public tables reference are seeded too
why: Otherwise a public table with an FK to them could not be seeded

decision: FK cycles broken by leaving a nullable key null; a cycle of NOT NULL keys falls to name order and fails visibly
why: The usual way out of mutually referencing tables; never a silent partial copy

decision: CHECK values from the constraint's own constants (strings; numbers n, n+1, n-1), at most 50 tries per row
why: Covers in(...), between, < and > without evaluating expressions; the same bound as the brief's value search

decision: A table counts as seeded if it has any rows; rows that already exist (migration seed data, triggers) are kept and fake rows are still tried
why: Brief: migrations' seed data is used too; a trigger-filled table must not stop the run

decision: A nullable column of an unsupported type is left null instead of blocking the table
why: Only a NOT NULL column without a value makes a table unseedable

decision: Arrays of generated types are now generated; T-02's unfillable fixture switched from text[] to point
why: text[] is common in Supabase apps; the fixture still needs a type that cannot be filled

decision: fake_row (write attacks) uses T-03's generators; a rolled-back trial insert only on tables with CHECKs
why: A trial insert uses up an identity value, which would shift T-02's pinned evidence ids

decision: Suite and mutants run in a private pid namespace and /tmp
why: The machine-wide residue checks flake while another builder runs rlsentry

decision: Migrations no longer go through psql: each file is split into statements by rlsentry (psql's rules: quotes, E'', dollar quotes, nested comments, parens, BEGIN ATOMIC) and sent through psycopg, one transaction and one connection per file
why: The verdict asked for no client that interprets backslash commands; the Supabase CLI also splits client-side and sends statements to the server; a connection per file keeps a migration's SET out of seeding

decision: Error line = line of the error's position when Postgres gives one, else the failing statement's first line (psql gave the line where the statement was sent)
why: More exact for multi-line statements; the line is now the only thing the splitter changes, since the server accepts a mis-split chunk

decision: Search path set once as the server default (postgres -c search_path) instead of ALTER DATABASE, plus PostgREST db-extra-search-path "public, extensions" and usage on schema extensions for anon/authenticated/service_role
why: ALTER DATABASE missed connections already open (the seeding one); a server default reaches every connection; PostgREST drops a schema its role cannot use

decision: Catch-all in cli.main: any other Exception prints "the run failed unexpectedly (Type: message); the copy was torn down" and exits 2, without a traceback
why: S-10 reserves exit 1 for exposed; teardown already runs through the Sandbox context manager

decision: auth.users gets the Supabase columns triggers typically read (instance_id, invited_at, confirmation_sent_at, recovery_sent_at, last_sign_in_at, is_super_admin, phone_confirmed_at, confirmed_at generated, banned_until, is_sso_user, deleted_at); token and secret columns left out
why: Smallest set that covers typical handle_new_user triggers; none of the left-out columns is read by triggers in Supabase's examples

decision: psql dropped from the required binaries

decision: T-06 written: protected = anon's effective policy false for every row tried, evaluated on the postgres connection as anon, rolled back; REST stays the only source of EXPOSED
why: Removes the 'verdict from inferred error' class by construction (the shilaycow-correct proposal)

decision: Cluster superuser renamed supabase_admin (as on Supabase); migrations, seeding, snapshot, restore and the write-clearing steps run as a LOGIN role named postgres (createrole, bypassrls, not superuser, no createdb)
why: Migrations name the postgres role (owner to postgres, grants); a separate connection, not SET ROLE, because migration code could RESET ROLE back to the superuser; createdb dropped as CREATE DATABASE cannot run in a migration's transaction

decision: The superuser's own connection searches pg_catalog only
why: A migration's public.format(text,text) was called by the superuser's catalogue query and ran COPY TO PROGRAM (reproduced on 5bab3db); another superuser-only route than the ticket's two

decision: pg_stat_statements pre-installed in extensions; untrusted extensions (adminpack, file_fdw, dblink, postgres_fdw) now stop the run with exit 2
why: Supabase ships pg_stat_statements and pulled schemas create it if not exists; the others reach the host or network and need a superuser

decision: T-05's docker backend must create the cluster superuser as supabase_admin (POSTGRES_USER) and let the postgres role log in
why: Migrations connect as postgres, which is no longer the superuser

decision: protected only for a clean RLS answer (2xx that changed nothing, or 42501); any other 4xx is cleared where possible and otherwise exit 2 naming table and operation, for all four operations
why: PostgreSQL checks INSERT/UPDATE policies before CHECK/unique/FK (seen in a probe: a row refused by both gets 42501), so such a refusal means the policy let the row through; same class as F1-F4

decision: Clearing the way: a seeded row a candidate collides with on a unique key is removed (make_room), and rows referencing a row whose DELETE hit 23503 are removed (detach_references), both as postgres in replica mode, then the request is sent once more; restore() puts everything back
why: Otherwise every RLS-off parent table and every 1:1 table keyed by auth.users would exit 2 on real projects; the basis says what was removed

decision: A trigger or policy raising for anon (400 P0001) stops the run (exit 2) instead of reading protected
why: It is a refusal, but not RLS's; consistent with the rule above

decision: Value search runs after any non-2xx first answer (not only 42501), always (also on tables with no insert policy), and counts every row sent toward the 50
why: A CHECK-rejected fake row is fixed by the same search; simpler than deciding when a search could help; lab tables with no policy say protected (12 rows tried)

decision: Candidate order: policy constants (all columns at once, then one at a time), CHECK constants, enum labels, seeded values, null; a constant goes to the columns named in its AND/OR term, numbers n, n+1, n-1 only to numeric columns; constants in terms naming no column are dropped
why: Covers status = 'pending', two-column policies and > / < bounds without evaluating expressions; auth.jwt() ->> 'role' constants cannot be put in a row anyway

decision: UPDATE may set columns that have a default; identity and generated columns never; a value equal to the target's own is skipped; key columns last; next column after a non-RLS refusal
why: F3's table with only defaulted columns was 'not attempted'; equal values made a 204 look like RLS (q"uote's varchar(4)); retrying covers F4 (ordering by uniqueness was redundant: its mutant survived, so it was removed)

decision: Text report shows INSERT: protected (N rows tried); evidence of a value-search find carries "source"
why: Ticket wording; JSON consumers get the source without parsing the basis

decision: T-03 fixtures changed: edge_cases pairs gains a nullable label column; statements' DO ALSO rule moved from a table to the view as DO INSTEAD, semi_audit dropped
why: pairs' only column can take no new value under its CHECK + unique, and PostgREST cannot write to a table with a DO ALSO rule: both now (correctly) exit 2, which those fixtures were not about

decision: lab_value_policy's status has a default ('draft'), so the row a form would send is refused
why: Shows value search setting a column the fresh fake row leaves to its default

decision: No test for a C-language function as a host route
why: As superuser PostgreSQL refuses libc anyway (no magic block), so no test could be seen to fail; non-superusers get permission denied for language c

decision: Candidate type check = an explicit cast of the constant to the column's type on the postgres connection; a failing cast drops the candidate
why: One rule covers interval/date, decimals and n±1 on integers, range tops and enum labels without per-type code; the cast runs no migration code as superuser

decision: An over-long varchar candidate is not caught by the cast (it truncates) but by PostgREST's 22001; any 22xxx answer is a rejected candidate that counts toward N rows tried, not an unclean answer and not the basis
why: A row was sent; the column could not hold it, which says nothing about the policy either way; the basis stays the last RLS refusal

decision: Column names are matched in a term with its string literals blanked
why: ->> 'role' reads a claim, not the role column (verdict D1)

decision: A 2xx INSERT with no new row seen as superuser is an unclean answer (search goes on; exit 2 if nothing else lands); evidence is always the row created
why: Finding 1: never EXPOSED on the sent row; same class as the rest of the task

decision: A retried DELETE compares with the rows read after the references were cleared
why: D3's test showed 7 rows reported deleted for 1: clearing parent_id made every row look gone

decision: D2 is proven by the number of rows tried (11, 12 with the role filter removed) on a table anon cannot insert into, not by a table the authenticated policy's constant would expose
why: Asserting protected for a table anon could in fact write would pin a false negative; the count shows the constant is never sent

decision: Findings 3 (UPDATE value search) and 4 (request cost) left as they are
why: Coordinator: they become later issues

decision: A 22xxx answer is a rejected candidate only if the row itself fails to read into the table row type (json_populate_record on the postgres connection, rolled back); otherwise it is unclean
why: The same SQLSTATE class comes from triggers and policies (verdict D4: 22023, 22012); reading the row as PostgREST does, with no trigger or policy, tells the value apart from the table's code

decision: INSERT reads protected only with at least one 42501; no RLS answer at all is exit 2 naming the table and INSERT
why: The basis is that answer, so an empty basis cannot occur

decision: The no-RLS-answer guard is tested with stand-in channel and inspector objects
why: No migration can make rlsentry's own fake row unholdable with no holdable candidate (every candidate keeps the base row's other values; seeded and null candidates always fit), so no real table reaches it

decision: This verdict's Findings 1 (_fits drops 0.5 instead of trying 1) and 2 (_fits commits a successful cast) left as they are
why: Not in this round's brief from the coordinator; Finding 1 is value-search recall (like Finding 3 of the first verdict), Finding 2 needs a domain whose CHECK has side effects

decision: Added a test where 42501s and one refusal from the table's own code (22023 or P0001) meet
why: The full mutant run showed M03 and M44 surviving: the no-RLS-answer guard also caught every earlier input, so neither the holds() check nor the unclean rule was proven on its own

decision: A 42501, or a 2xx UPDATE/DELETE that changed nothing, is RLS's (or a grant's) answer only if the same write, sent again by the sandbox on the postgres connection as SET ROLE anon with anon's claims, session_replication_role = replica and rolled back, is refused the same way (42501, or nothing changed)
why: The coordinator's suggested design; a trigger can raise 42501 with RLS's own message, so neither code nor text can tell; the recheck rules out (non-ALWAYS) triggers

decision: The recheck also covers a 2xx UPDATE/DELETE that changed nothing (a BEFORE trigger returning null for anon), beyond the 42501 the verdict names
why: Same class: a silent skip by the table's code looked like RLS filtering the row

decision: Known limits of the recheck: ALWAYS triggers, column defaults and RI checks still run or are off as replica mode sets them, and the claims are {role: anon, iss: rlsentry} without exp; a 42501 from an ALWAYS trigger or a default would still read as RLS's
why: No such case in the verdicts; replica mode is the switch the coordinator named; a fuller recheck would need to drop and recreate triggers

decision: lab_value_policy's evidence id goes 7 -> 8
why: The recheck's rolled-back insert uses an identity value (sequences survive rollback; verdict Finding 1, left alone as asked)

decision: Tests pin to the postgres connection, and to a rolled-back transaction, every Inspector method that casts to a column type: holds, _fits (via value_sources), would_change, fake_row, as_anon; make_room only to the connection (its delete is meant to stay until restore()); _fits and would_change no longer commit
why: A domain CHECK calling a migration function runs on any such cast; the probe function resets role first, so a superuser connection that had SET ROLE anon is caught too

decision: statement_timeout 30s on the postgres connection only (seeding, restore, inspector work); migration connections have none
why: A migration may legitimately run long (data backfills); the inspector and seeding statements are small; the test lowers it to 1s

decision: Verdict Finding 1 (nextval and advisory locks surviving rollback) left alone
why: Coordinator: confined to the copy

decision: The domain-CHECK probe resets role before COPY
why: M59 (as_anon on the superuser connection) survived otherwise: SET ROLE anon hid the superuser from a probe that did not reset it, though migration code can

decision: Local process code moved from sandbox.py to rlsentry/backends/local.py; sandbox.py keeps setup SQL, migrations, seeding, nonce and PostgREST settings for both backends
why: One seam; T-04's role change in the shared SQL reaches docker without duplication

decision: PostgREST joins the db container's network namespace (--network container:), both ports published on the db container at 127.0.0.1
why: No docker network to create or leak; the database is never reachable except on 127.0.0.1

decision: Docker backend refuses a daemon not on this machine (DOCKER_HOST or context endpoint not unix:// or npipe://); auto falls back to local
why: A remote daemon's 127.0.0.1 is not ours: the channel would reach whatever listens on our loopback port

decision: After docker run, docker port must show exactly our two ports on 127.0.0.1, else exit 2
why: Proves the binding at the daemon, not only in our argv

decision: Startup sweep removes only labelled containers whose owner (host/pid/start time) is gone; other hosts, live runs and unreadable labels are kept
why: Brief: two runs at once get separate copies; a reused pid must not keep a dead run's containers

decision: Each backend sweeps only its own leftovers at startup (a docker run does not sweep local markers, or the reverse)
why: A local run need not touch the docker CLI; leftovers are swept by the next run of the same backend

decision: --backend defaults to auto; the fallback is announced on stderr
why: Design D-1 makes docker the default and auto the fallback path; a silent fallback would hide which copy was attacked

decision: The conftest rlsentry() helper passes --backend local unless the test names one
why: Existing tests look for local pids and markers; on a machine with a daemon, auto would pick docker

decision: JWT secret passed to PostgREST as -e NAME with the value in the docker client's environment
why: Keeps it off every command line (ps, transcripts)

decision: Postgres connect and PostgREST ready deadlines raised from 30 s to 60 s, for both backends
why: The postgres image runs initdb on first start

decision: Pulled images are kept after a run; containers and their anonymous volumes (rm -f -v) are removed
why: Images are a cache, not run state; re-pulling each run would hit Docker Hub's 429

decision: Docker backend proven against tests/fakedocker.py (local processes as containers); real-daemon lab test skipped here, reported as a gap
why: No daemon in this environment and Docker Hub rate-limits pulls; a driven check against the real images was impossible

decision: docker run held against SIGINT/SIGTERM (signals blocked) and docker CLI in its own session; proven with a fake daemon that finishes creating after its client dies
why: Otherwise teardown can look for the container before the daemon has created it

decision: start_db takes the superuser's name from sandbox.SUPERUSER (local initdb -U, docker POSTGRES_USER)
why: Orchestrator heads-up: T-04 makes supabase_admin the superuser; one constant for both backends

decision: Did not merge T-04 (not yet in task/anon-probe); rehearsed the merge in a scratch worktree: 124 passed, 1 skipped
